THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.t: THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.short: She sells tomatoes... She steals destiny. Ama Mensah 22, poor tomato seller at Kaneshie, watches customers leave her for Madam Darkoa whose tomatoes glow green and never spoil. Her blind grandmother shouts: This is not tomato, this is destiny!
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.long: Kaneshie Market, 4am. Ama Mensah, 22, beautiful hardworking tomato seller from Agbogbloshie, feeds her blind grandmother Grandma Esi and jobless brother Kofi. When strange old woman Madam Darkoa appears selling glowing red tomatoes that never spoil, Ama's business dies. Blind Grandma Esi touches one and screams it is destiny theft - each tomato is a trapped human star. 99 destinies already trapped, Ama will be number 100. With Mallam Musah's black soap and white handkerchief, Ama must sell the cursed tomato back to the Market Witch on Tuesday full market day. Green lightning, yellow glowing eyes, blood inside tomato - Ghanaian spiritual folk tale about envy, hard work and destiny. Pure Ghana names, Kaneshie, Agbogbloshie, Makola. Moral: Not every shining business is clean.
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.full:
NARRATOR: Kaneshie Market, 4am, dark, cold, only torch lights. Ama Mensah, 22 years, beautiful, hardworking, very poor tomato seller, carries heavy basket on head from Agbogbloshie.

AMA MENSAH: Grandma Esi, today I will sell all my tomatoes by God's grace. I am tired of poverty. Kofi trotro no work, you blind, I am the only one. But I will not steal, I will not do juju. I will work hard with clean hands.

GRANDMA ESI: My granddaughter Ama, my spirit is not comfortable today. I am blind with eyes but I see with spirit. Not all red is tomato. Not all shining market is clean. Some traders sell more than goods. They sell destiny. Be careful in Kaneshie today.

NARRATOR: Same market, Madam Darkoa, 53, The Market Witch, sells reddest tomatoes that glow green at night and never spoil. Customers leave Ama.

AMA MENSAH: Why customers no dey buy from me today? My tomatoes fresh from Agbogbloshie this morning. Something is wrong.

AFIA: Ama, make I try buy one from Madam Darkoa and see. Maybe her own get chemical?

GRANDMA ESI: AHHHH! This is not tomato! This is destiny! This is human star! She is stealing people's stars!

GRANDMA ESI: That woman is a market witch! In 1973, she was cursed by Nana Okomfo for using 3 children for money rituals at Tano River. When you eat her tomato, she exchanges your good luck for her bad luck.

AFIA: Too late Grandma! I ate yesterday! My boyfriend broke up, my hair falling, my GHC 200 disappeared!

AMA MENSAH: I must confront her! Tonight midnight at Kaneshie when market empty!

NARRATOR: Midnight, 12:05am, empty Kaneshie Market. Ama hides behind Queen Yaa stall. Sees Madam Darkoa holding floating tomato with green lightning, chanting.

MADAM DARKOA: Give me your market... give me your marriage... give me your children... give me your womb... I give you tomatoes...

MADAM DARKOA: You small girl... you want to know my secret? Come closer. Buy one tomato. Just one.

NARRATOR: Ama runs to Makola to Mallam Musah, 80 years old.

MALLAM MUSAH: Ama Mensah, your destiny star already dim. You touched her stall last week. She started taking small small. Take black soap and white handkerchief. Don't eat anything in market for 7 days. Bring me one glowing tomato at 12 midnight on 7th day.

NARRATOR: 7th day, midnight, heavy rain. Ama steals one tomato. Tomato heavy like stone, cold like ice, inside baby crying.

AMA MENSAH: Eiii! This tomato heavy! I hear baby crying inside! Blood comes out, not water!

MALLAM MUSAH: Look! Each tomato is trapped destiny! She trapped 99 destinies. You will be number 100 and she will become young again!

NARRATOR: Meanwhile Kofi, Ama brother, greedy, jobless, goes to Madam Darkoa.

KOFI: Madam Darkoa, make me rich. I will bring you my sister.

MADAM DARKOA: Bring Ama hair and pant. I will make you rich in one night.

KOFI: Forgive me sister, I need money.

AMA MENSAH: Dreaming, woman with green hands strangling her.

MALLAM MUSAH: Only one way left. Kofi betrayed you. She has your pant. You must sell cursed tomato back to her on Tuesday market day, when market fullest, when queen mother Queen Yaa is there.

NARRATOR: Tuesday, Kaneshie full like Christmas. Queen Yaa inspecting stalls. Ama holding cursed tomato wrapped in white handkerchief.

AMA MENSAH: Madam Darkoa, good morning. I want to sell you tomato. Very fresh. Better than yours.

MADAM DARKOA: You small girl want to sell tomato to tomato seller? Give me.

MADAM DARKOA: AHHH! WHAT HAVE YOU DONE!

NARRATOR: Green lightning explodes from Madam Darkoa mouth, eyes, hands! Throat glows green, skin cracks like rotten tomato. All trapped destinies fly out as bright green lights. Market women who poor suddenly get customers.

MADAM DARKOA: If I go down, you go down with me!

AMA MENSAH: I reject you in Jesus name and Allah name! Kaneshie market is for hard work, not witchcraft!

GRANDMA ESI: Return to where you came from, witch! 

NARRATOR: GBOOOM! Madam Darkoa melts into pile of rotten tomatoes, green smoke to sky. Only her stall burns with green fire.

QUEEN YAA: From today, Madam Darkoa spot given to Ama Mensah for bravery! We pray every Monday!

KOFI: Ama, forgive me, I was greedy.

AMA MENSAH: I forgive you brother, but return GHC 5000 to Mallam Musah.

NARRATOR: One month later, Ama biggest tomato business in Kaneshie. Mr Joseph gives her cold store. She marries Mr Joseph son. At night, when Ama closes stall, sometimes she still sees one green tomato glowing under Madam Darkoa old table... She never touches it. THE END.

MORAL: Not every shining business clean. Hard work with small profit better than quick money that steals future.

SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.t: SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.short: 22-year-old Choima from Onitsha sells zobo to pay her sick mother's N450k hospital bill. An agent promises $500/month house help job in Saudi. But she is sold for $4000, passport seized, phone taken, forced to work 19 hours daily as a slave.
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.long: Nollywood drama about human trafficking and Saudi housemaid wahala. Choima, beautiful Anambra girl from Onitsha Main Market, pays N350k to agent Alhaja Kudirat for Riyadh job. No contract, no NAPTIP clearance, passport collected at Lagos airport. In Saudi, madam Mama Um Khalid seizes phone, locks gate, beats her, no salary for 6 months. Based on true stories of Nigerian girls in Saudi, NAPTIP warning, illegal migration from Anambra to Saudi Arabia. Pure Igbo names, Onitsha, Agege training house, Murtala Muhammed Airport, Riyadh, Jeddah. Moral: Not every abroad is greener, verify agent.
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.full:
NARRATOR: Onitsha Main Market, Anambra. Noon. Hot sun. Choima, 22, beautiful, fair-skinned, natural hair, sells zobo and meat pie to feed four younger brothers and sisters. Father died. Mother sick, leg swollen, on mat at home.

CHOIMA: Mama, I will sell everything today. I need N450,000 for your hospital at Nnamdi Azikiwe Teaching Hospital. God will provide.

MAMA CHOIMA: [crying] My daughter, don't stress. I am tired.

NARRATOR: A black Lexus parks. Alhaja Kudirat steps out. Gold, expensive lace.

ALHAJA KUDIRAT: My daughter, you are beautiful and hardworking. I have house help job in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Salary $500 per month, almost N800,000. Many Nigerian girls are there enjoying. They drive Benz.

CHOIMA: Aunty, I saw on TikTok they beat house helps in Saudi. My friend from Asaba went and never came back.

ALHAJA KUDIRAT: That is Dubai, not Saudi. Saudi is good Islamic country. Very safe. My daughter is there. Look [shows video of girl dancing in Riyadh mall].

NARRATOR: Choima thinks of mother crying, brothers not in school, shop rent unpaid. She says yes. Sells mother's wrapper shop, borrows from church, pays N350,000 processing fee.

NARRATOR: Lagos, Agege, small house, 2 weeks training. Clean toilet with hands, wear abaya, say Naam Mama. No contract. No NAPTIP paper. No embassy meeting.

NARRATOR: Murtala Muhammed Airport. Alhaja collects passport.

ALHAJA KUDIRAT: I will keep it safe. Your madam will give you Iqama.

NARRATOR: First airplane ever. Lagos to Jeddah to Riyadh, 6 hours, black abaya, crying. Riyadh Airport, Mama Um Khalid, 50 years, big, seven children, three-storey house, collects phone.

MAMA UM KHALID: No phone. No Nigerian boyfriend. Only work.

NARRATOR: Her room is a small store. No bed. Thin mat beside rice bags. No fan. Day 1 suffering: Wake 4am, cook breakfast for ten, clean 5 bedrooms, 4 toilets, wash clothes by hand, cook Kabsa for fifteen, watch five children, wash plates midnight. 5am to 1am. Nineteen hours daily. Feet swollen.

MAMA UM KHALID: Yalla! Yalla! Fast! Donkey! [beats with mop stick]

CHOIMA: [crying inside toilet she cleans] God, in Onitsha I was free.

CHOIMA: Mama, please my salary? My mother is sick in Anambra.

MAMA UM KHALID: Salary after three months! I paid your agent $4000 for you! You are my property now!

NARRATOR: Choima understands. Alhaja sold her for $4000. She is not worker. She is slave. Three months, no salary, no phone, passport seized, gate locked with camera, Iqama not done.

NARRATOR: Sixth month, night, madam's 20-year-old son tries to enter her small store room.

CHOIMA: [screams, bites hand, locks door] Leave me!

NARRATOR: Reports to madam. Madam beats her again.

MAMA UM KHALID: You seducing my son! Bad Nigerian girl! [locks her outside in 48-degree heat, no water whole day]

CHOIMA: [kneeling outside in hot sun, black abaya, sweating, looking at sky] God, I left Anambra to help my mother. Now I am slave in Saudi. Who will save me? [hides small paper in underwear, number copied from airport toilet wall: +966 11 442 8624 Nigerian Embassy Riyadh]

NARRATOR: Night. Whisper through fence. Fatima from Ibadan, next compound.

FATIMA: Choima, don't cry. Many Nigerian girls here one year no salary. We will run to embassy together on Friday when madam goes to mosque...

TO BE CONTINUED IN PART 2 - THE FRIDAY ESCAPE.

HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.t: HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DAY
HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.short: Adaeze's Lagos wedding with 400 guests turns to chaos. At 6am on wedding day, she catches fiancé Emeka naked with her younger sister Chiamaka on their wedding bed. He says she is boring. She takes microphone and shocks everyone.
HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.long: Nigerian wedding betrayal story Lagos, 400 guests, bride catches groom sleeping with sister on wedding day. Adaeze was to marry Emeka in Lekki Lagos, white wedding gown, 400 guests already seated. Emeka slept with her blood sister Chiamaka 10 minutes before wedding. She records confession, plays on microphone, walks out as queen. Based on true Lagos wedding wahala, sister betrayal, fiancé cheating. Pure Nigerian names, Lekki, Lagos, Dangote contract. Moral: Sisterhood, self-worth. High search: Nigeria wedding betrayal story, sister slept with my fiancé on wedding day, Lagos wedding scandal.
HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.full:
NARRATOR: Lagos, 6am, wedding day. Adaeze, 26, beautiful, in white wedding gown, makeup done, 400 guests already seated in hall outside. Tradition: go pray with fiancé before wedding.

ADAEZE: [knocks] Emeka, baby, let's pray before we go to church.

NARRATOR: Door locked. Moaning inside. Adaeze pushes door hard. Sees it. Fiancé Emeka, naked, on top of her own younger sister Chiamaka, in their wedding bed.

ADAEZE: Jesus Christ! Emeka! Chiamaka! What is this!

CHIAMAKA: [shouts, covering body] Sister please, it's not what you think! He forced me!

EMEKA: [looks at Adaeze, no shame] Adaeze, you were always too boring in bed. Your sister taught me yesterday what you couldn't in 3 years.

NARRATOR: Wedding in 3 hours. Mother dancing outside, spraying money. Adaeze standing in wedding gown, watching sister dress quickly, crying.

NARRATOR: Adaeze walks to hall. White gown dragging. Makeup smudged with tears. DJ playing. Mother dancing with aunties. Everyone shouting Omo iyawo ti de!

ADAEZE: [collects microphone, DJ stops music, voice shaking] Good morning everyone. Thank you for coming to my wedding. But there will be no wedding today.

NARRATOR: Silence. 400 people quiet.

MAMA ADAEZE: Adaeze! What are you saying?!

ADAEZE: [points at entrance] This man Emeka that I was supposed to marry, I caught him 10 minutes ago sleeping with my own blood sister Chiamaka. On my wedding bed. On my wedding day.

NARRATOR: Hall scatters! Jesu! Ewo! Oloriburuku! Mother faints.

CHIAMAKA: [runs, kneels, holds Adaeze leg] Sister, he forced me! He said if I don't sleep with him, he will cancel wedding and disgrace you!

EMEKA: [laughs] So? At least now you know truth. I never loved you, Adaeze. I only wanted your father's land in Lekki. Your sister is sweeter.

ADAEZE: [raises phone, red light blinking]

EMEKA: What recording? You bluffing.

ADAEZE: [plays loud on microphone] EMEKA VOICE: You were always too boring in bed. Your sister taught me yesterday what you couldn't in 3 years.

NARRATOR: Two police officers, father's friends for security, walk in. Papa Adaeze stands, agbada shaking.

PAPA ADAEZE: Emeka, I gave you my daughter, and you repay me like this?

EMEKA: [kneels instantly] Sir, please! It was devil! Adaeze, biko, forgive me!

ADAEZE: [looks at both, tears but smiling] Officers, don't arrest him. Let him go.

EVERYONE: WHAT?!

ADAEZE: Let him go, because real punishment is he will watch me become millionaire without him. And Chiamaka, you will never enter my house again until you learn what sisterhood means.

NARRATOR: Adaeze removes wedding gown in front of everyone, wears jeans under it, walks out of own wedding hall like queen.

NARRATOR: 3 months later. Emeka loses job. Chiamaka comes begging. Adaeze gets contract with Dangote.

NARRATOR: Last week, Emeka sends text.

EMEKA: Adaeze, I am dying. Please come see me. I have secret about Chiamaka you need to know...

END OF SEASON 1. Should I write Season 2? Comment YES!

THE HIDDEN SECRET PART 1.short: Ada 20 and Amara 18 live as billionaire Chief Chibike's princesses in Lekki. At mother's burial in Enugu, uncle stops coffin — inside dead mother's legs, black wooden box locked with padlock. Inside: 2 birth certificates and letter saying Chibike is not their father, 3 men Chidi, Emeka, Ifeanyi — one is real father, plus 50M land in Eko Atlantic.
THE HIDDEN SECRET PART 1.long: Nollywood family secret story Lagos Lekki to Enugu. Ada Okoro 20 and Amara Okoro 18 bury mother Mama Nkechi 48 at family house Enugu. Mortuary box found between legs, dead hand locked around it, had to break fingers. Inside black wooden box: 2 birth certificates and handwritten letter revealing billionaire father Chibike not biological father, mother cheated with 3 men Chidi, Emeka, Ifeanyi, one is father, plus 2 plots Eko Atlantic 50 Million Naira for real father. Ifeanyi is Papa Chibike's closest business partner 15 years Alaba importation, sleeps in house, paid school fees, now last name on letter least suspected. Who is real father? DNA shock coming. Pure Igbo names, Lekki, Enugu, Alaba, Eko Atlantic. Moral: secrets, betrayal, business partner twist. High search: hidden secret mother left in coffin, mother letter after death Nigerian story, billionaire father not my father.
THE HIDDEN SECRET PART 1.full:
NARRATOR: Lagos, Lekki, billionaire mansion. Ada 20, Amara 18, lived 20 years with father Chief Chibike, 3 cars, housemaids, princesses.

NARRATOR: Tuesday, mother Mama Nkechi, 48, died. Saturday, burial at family house Enugu. Pastor prayed, pallbearers about to close coffin.

CHIDI: [shouts] STOP! Don't close it! Chibike, we cannot bury her with that box! If we bury her with it, this whole family will die before 7 days! I saw it in my dream!

NARRATOR: Everyone turns. Uncle Chidi shaking. Look inside coffin, under Mama's white burial dress, between her legs, small black wooden box, locked with gold padlock. Nobody put it there. Mortuary man didn't see it when he dressed her.

AMARA: [tries to pull] Ada, help me!

NARRATOR: Mama's dead hand holding tight, fingers locked around it. Whole funeral screams Jesus! Eii! Had to break her fingers to remove it.

NARRATOR: Back of house, Papa Chibike says break with hammer.

CHIBIKE: Break it with hammer!

NARRATOR: Inside not money, not jewelry. 2 birth certificates and 1 handwritten letter.

ADA: [reads] Birth Certificate 1: ADA OKORO - Age 20. Birth Certificate 2: AMARA OKORO - Age 18.

NARRATOR: And letter, mother's handwriting.

MAMA NKECHI: [letter voice] My dear Ada and Amara, forgive me. Your father Chibike is not your biological father. For 20 years he raised you thinking you are his. I cheated behind your father with 3 men — Chidi, Emeka and Ifeanyi — one of them is your biological father of you 2, look for him. Under my bed in Lagos is the land documents — 2 plots at Eko Atlantic worth 50 MILLION NAIRA. The land is not for Chibike, it is for your real father. Find him. — Mama Nkechi

NARRATOR: Ada looks up. Papa Chibike, billionaire father who raised her 20 years, already running away from graveyard, crying.

CHIBIKE: [crying, running] Nkechi! Why?

NARRATOR: Uncle Chidi faints.

CHIDI: [faints] Jesus! Ada is mine?

EMEKA: [shouts] That is a lie! Amara is my daughter!

NARRATOR: At gate, Ifeanyi standing. Last name on letter. One everybody will never suspect.

IFEANYI: Ada, what is inside box? Don't worry, I will help you people find truth. I know all these men, I will call them for DNA. I am with you.

NARRATOR: Ifeanyi is not just family friend. He is Papa Chibike's closest business partner for 15 years! They do importation together at Alaba! He sleeps in house! He helped Mama when sick! Paid school fees! Like brother to Papa Chibike! They hug him. Think he is helping. Never suspect him at all. How can Ifeanyi, Papa's business partner, be our father?

NARRATOR: TO BE CONTINUED IN PART 2: WE DID DNA FOR THE 3 MEN — THE RESULT SHOCKED THE WHOLE VILLAGE!

END OF PART 1.

AMARA.short: Amara lost mom at 8. Step-mom stops her school in Primary 4, makes her house girl. At 19 she meets rich CEO Bright who teaches her ABC. From market girl to best graduate.
AMARA.long: Ghana Cinderella story. Amara 19, illiterate house girl, mocked by step-mom Mama Esther & step-sister Esther. She meets Bright 27, rich CEO who teaches her to read 7pm daily. She enrolls adult school, fails, then becomes best graduating student. Wedding + forgiveness. Wicked stepmother to graduate.
AMARA.full:
NARRATOR: PART 1 - HOW IT ALL STARTED

SCENE 1
NARRATOR: Amara's mother dies. Little Amara 8 years crying on grave. Papa Amara broken. Mama Esther appears at funeral, acting nice, consoling Papa Amara. She has plan already.

VOICEOVER: When Amara lost her mother, Mama Esther saw an opportunity. Not to be a mother... but to be an owner.

SCENE 2
NARRATOR: 6 months later, Mama Esther moves in with Esther. First week nice. Second week, removes Amara from school.

MAMA ESTHER: [to Papa Amara] Why waste money? Girls will marry. Let Esther go, she is brilliant.

PAPA AMARA: Okay.

NARRATOR: Papa agrees. Amara stops in Primary 4. Becomes house help in her father's house.

SCENE 3 - 11 YEARS OF HELL
NARRATOR: Amara now 19. Wakes 4am, sweeps, cooks, fetches water, goes to market. Cannot read price, market women cheat her. Esther same age, goes to school, wears nice clothes, uses iPhone.

ESTHER: Amara, read this letter for me na [laughs] Oh I forgot, you can't read. Illiterate!

MAMA ESTHER: Your mother gave birth to a house girl.

NARRATOR: PART 2 - THE ARRIVAL OF BRIGHT

SCENE 4
NARRATOR: Amara from market, carrying heavy food stuffs. Man in car spill water on Amara. Handsome man - Bright. Owns biggest company's in city.

BRIGHT: Hey, let me help you.

NARRATOR: He carries it. Amara shy.

SCENE 5
NARRATOR: Bright starts seeing her everyday. Notices she never goes to school. Writes number on paper.

BRIGHT: Call me if you need anything.

AMARA: [holds paper upside down, tears] I... I don't know how to read.

NARRATOR: Bright shocked. Understands everything instantly.

SCENE 6
NARRATOR: Mama Esther and Esther see Bright dropping Amara home. Jealousy starts DEEPLY.

MAMA ESTHER: Look at this illiterate girl. She wants to snatch a rich CEO? Never!

ESTHER: Mummy, he is supposed to be mine! I'm the educated one! He can't marry a girl who can't write her name.

NARRATOR: From that day, increase wickedness. Lock food, beat her, tell Papa Amara Amara following men.

SCENE 7
NARRATOR: Mama Esther tries to slap Amara for talking to Bright. Bright appears at gate at exact time and holds Mama Esther's hand.

BRIGHT: [angry first time] Don't you ever touch her again! If you want to fight, fight me!

NARRATOR: Papa Amara sees this. First time, sees Mama Esther's real face. Amara runs and hugs Bright, crying.

NARRATOR: PART 3 - LOVE AND EDUCATION

SCENE 8
NARRATOR: Bright takes Amara to coffee shop.

BRIGHT: I love you not because you can read, but because your heart is pure. But I will help you read.

NARRATOR: Every evening 7pm-9pm after work, teaches A-B-C. Amara cries, struggles, but learns fast because hungry for knowledge. Mama Esther sends people to spy, telling village people Amara is now bad girl sleeping in man's house.

SCENE 9
NARRATOR: Mama Esther's FINAL WICKED PLAN. Arranges marriage for Amara to 62-year-old drunkard man in village for 2 goats and money, without Papa Amara knowing. Old man comes to pick Amara one morning. Amara screams. Esther videoing laughing.

BRIGHT: [arrives with police and Papa Amara]

PAPA AMARA: Over my dead body! No one marries off my daughter!

NARRATOR: Papa finally chases Mama Esther out of bedroom tells her stay in visitors room. That night tells Amara.

PAPA AMARA: My daughter, forgive me. Go with Bright. Go and be what your mother wanted you to be.

NARRATOR: Amara leaves home with one bag.

SCENE 10
NARRATOR: Amara enrolls Adult Evening School. Oldest in SHS 1 class. Students laugh. Teachers pity. Fails first exams. Wants to quit.

BRIGHT: [buys books, cooks, waits outside school in rain] The girl they called illiterate will graduate one day.

NARRATOR: Reads all night. For 3 years, no party, no makeup, only books. Mama Esther and Esther keep coming to school to mock.

MAMA ESTHER: See illiterate girl wearing uniform!

NARRATOR: PART 4 - THE PAYBACK - GRADUATION & WEDDING

SCENE 11 - GRADUATION DAY
NARRATOR: Big hall. Name called.

ANNOUNCER: AMARA OWUSU - BEST GRADUATING STUDENT, ARTS DEPARTMENT!

NARRATOR: Amara walks in graduation gown, glowing, confident, speaks fluent English. Everyone stands claps. Papa Amara in wheelchair crying, Bright filming proud smile. Outside gate, Mama Esther and Esther watching far, wearing old clothes. Esther couldn't even pass WASSCE.

ESTHER: [crying] Mummy, that should have been me!

SCENE 12 - THE PROPOSAL
NARRATOR: Same night after graduation, Bright takes Amara to house decorated with flowers. Kneels.

BRIGHT: Amara, I met you when you couldn't write your name. Today you are a graduate. Will you marry me?

AMARA: [cries] YES!

SCENE 13 - THE WEDDING
NARRATOR: Big Ghanaian traditional wedding + white wedding. Amara stunning. Bright handsome. Papa Amara gives her away, healthy now. Mama Esther and Esther come late, not invited, in tattered clothes, to beg. Kneel before Amara.

MAMA ESTHER: Amara, forgive us. We were wicked. We tried to destroy you because of jealousy.

ESTHER: Sister, please forgive me. I mocked you. Now I have nothing.

AMARA: [in wedding gown, lifts them, hugs] I forgave you long time ago. If you didn't keep me illiterate, I would never have met Bright who taught me. Your wickedness led me to my destiny.

NARRATOR: Everyone cries. Bright hugs Amara.

FINAL TEXT ON SCREEN: They tried to keep her down because of jealousy, but God lifted her up. Forgiveness is the final victory.

THE RIVER BRIDE.short: Village girl Adaeze 19 is chosen as bride for River God to save village from 7 months drought. She loves hunter Emeka. Marry a god for rain or die for love?
THE RIVER BRIDE.long: Umunzu village near River Niger, no rain 7 months. Elders say river demands a pure bride. Adaeze, farmer's daughter 19 with mark on left shoulder, is chosen. She loves Emeka the hunter. At midnight she meets River God, handsome man from water. He gives choice: marry me for rain and let Emeka live, or village becomes desert 7 years. She enters river, rain falls. Now goddess with one night a year to return to land.
THE RIVER BRIDE.full:
NARRATOR: In a small village called Umunzu, near River Niger, rain had not fallen for seven months. Farms were dry. Children were crying. The elders were afraid.

IGWE OKORO: Our river is angry! Who will save us?

ELDER OKAFOR: Igwe, the old priestess said it before — the river demands a bride. A pure girl to marry the water.

NARRATOR: In that village, there was a 19-year-old girl, Adaeze. She was very beautiful, kind, and the only child of a poor farmer. She was in love with Emeka, the hunter's son.

ADAEZE: Emeka, when will you come and marry me? My father is waiting.

EMEKA: Adaeze, I am gathering money. By the next market day, you will be my wife. I promise you.

NARRATOR: That same night, the Igwe called all the beautiful girls to the palace.

IGWE OKORO: Our priestess has spoken. The river has chosen. A girl born on Saturday, with a mark on her left shoulder — she will be the River Bride, or we will all die.

PRIESTESS NNEKA: She is the one! Adaeze, daughter of Obinna! Tomorrow by midnight, you must go to the river with a white wrapper. The River God will come to take you.

OBINNA: My only child! No! Take my farm! Take my life!

ADAEZE: Father, if I don't go, the whole village will die of hunger.

EMEKA: Adaeze, I will not allow it! I will fight the River God!

NARRATOR: At midnight, Adaeze walked to the river alone. She wore a white wrapper and was crying. The water started spinning. A tall, handsome man came out from the water, his eyes shining like diamonds.

RIVER GOD: Adaeze... I have waited 100 years for you. You have finally come. Come and be my queen. Your village will have rain forever.

ADAEZE: I don't want to be a queen! I love Emeka! I am human!

RIVER GOD: Love? Human love dies in one year. Mine is forever. If you refuse me, your village will become a desert for seven years.

EMEKA: Leave her! She is mine!

NARRATOR: Emeka attacked the River God, but his cutlass just passed through water. The River God laughed.

RIVER GOD: Foolish boy! You cannot kill water!

RIVER GOD: I give you a choice, Adaeze. Marry me tonight, and I will give your village rain, and I will let this boy live. If you refuse, I will take you by force, and I will kill him and your father.

ADAEZE: If I become the river bride, will my people live?

RIVER GOD: They will prosper more than before. And you... you will never die. You will become a goddess.

NARRATOR: Adaeze made her decision. She kissed Emeka for the last time.

ADAEZE: Tell my father that I love him. And tell the village... I did it for them.

EMEKA: ADAEZE!!!!

NARRATOR: Adaeze entered the river. The water closed. Immediately, heavy rain started falling! Thunder! The dry river started flowing full! People started dancing! But deep inside the water, Adaeze did not die. She sat on a throne of gold and pearls. The River God placed a crown on her head.

RIVER GOD: You are now the River Bride. But you are sad.

ADAEZE: My heart is still on land.

RIVER GOD: I will give you power. Once every year, on the night you became my bride, you can return to land for one night as a human. But if you ever sleep with a human man that night, both of you will turn to river stones forever.

NARRATOR: One year later, that night came. Adaeze returned to land, beautiful and shining. Emeka was still waiting by the river side. He never married.

EMEKA: Adaeze? Is that you? You have come back!

ADAEZE: Emeka! I have only one night!

NARRATOR: They hugged, they cried, and they talked all night. Emeka wanted to touch her, but Adaeze told him about the curse. So they just held hands till morning. Every year, Adaeze came. The village now worships her. They call her Mama Rain. Children bring white flowers for her. But last year, something happened. Emeka has grown a little older, but Adaeze is still 19. And the River God has become jealous...

RIVER GOD: Adaeze, you love him more than me. This year, if you go to meet him, I will not let you return. You will die.

ADAEZE: Then let me die! I want one night to be a human wife, not a goddess!

NARRATOR: What will happen this year? Will Adaeze risk death to be with Emeka for one night? Will the River God destroy the village again? TO BE CONTINUED IN RIVER BRIDE PART 2...
